Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • The equipment list carries 35 items; each datasheet takes one of them to a vendor.
  • A blocked-in pump sets $P_d$ on the desalters (P-1, 1550) and the heater coil (P-2, 2650 kPa g).
  • Low-pressure items get the +170 kPa term: V-1 250, V-4 200 kPa g. V-4 sits below its PSV-102 set pressure, 350.

Part 2

How thick a shell, and how many exchanger shells?

Part 2 · the plan

A code formula for the wall, a correction factor for the area

  1. The ASME VIII formulasshell and head thickness, MAWP
  2. Size a walldesalter V-3: 22 mm plate
  3. The F factorE-1 and E-14 need two shells
  4. The preheat trainwhat those shells look like

Step 1 · ASME VIII Div 1, UG-27 and UG-32

From design pressure to plate thickness

1$R = D/2 + CA$  (corroded radius)
2$t_{shell} = \dfrac{PR}{SE - 0.6P} + CA$
3$t_{head} = \dfrac{PD}{2SE - 0.2P} + CA$  (2:1 ellipsoidal)
4$MAWP = \dfrac{SE\,(t - CA)}{R + 0.6(t - CA)}$

How it is used

$P$ is $P_d$ plus liquid head. Round $t$ up to the next standard plate; it never goes below $D/1000 + 2.5 + CA$.

Valid while $P \le 0.385\,SE$. $S$ here is an approximate SA-516-70 value; a design reads ASME II-D.

rating$Q = U A F\,\Delta T_{lm}$,   $F \ge 0.8$

Step 4 · the preheat train

Shell-and-tube exchangers, stacked two high

TEMA AES: removable channel at one end, floating head at the other, so the bundle can be pulled for cleaning. AI-generated illustration (Gemini).

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • The desalter needs 17.3 mm for pressure, 22 mm plate with corrosion allowance; MAWP 1705, hydrotest 2217 kPa g.
  • At low pressure the minimum thickness governs: V-1 gets 10 mm.
  • E-1 ($F$ 0.73) and E-14 ($F$ 0.61) need two shells in series; the other eleven pass with one.

Where do the documents disagree?

Step 3 · interactive · engineering queries

What does each query ask someone to decide?

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • The 60 m³ bottoms holdup of the model costs 6.6 m of column height; 10 minutes would need 1.9 m.
  • 78 of 86 checks pass; the 8 failures are on V-4 relief and on high alarms above the design temperature.
  • Each failure is written up as an engineering query with its references, not corrected silently.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Set design pressure from the worst case, including a blocked-in pump.

2

Keep every relief set pressure and high alarm inside the design conditions.

3

Check the F factor before trusting a single-shell exchanger.

4

Turn each document mismatch into a written engineering query.
